name: Hezron
overview: Hezron was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known as the son of Perez and grandson of Judah, as recorded in Genesis 46:12. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as part of the early Israelite genealogy during the patriarchal period. Hezron is also associated with the Hezronite clan mentioned in Numbers 26:21.
namesAndTitles: The name Hezron means 'enclosure' and is a proper name not given directly by God, as noted in Genesis 46:12. This name likely reflects a characteristic or symbolic meaning relevant to his identity within the family lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hezron as the son of Perez. Additional inferred relationships include his father Ram (Ruth 4:19), and further descendants such as Jerahmeel, Chelubai (1 Chronicles 2:9), Segub (1 Chronicles 2:21), and Ashhur (1 Chronicles 2:24). He is also inferred to have been the husband of Abijah (1 Chronicles 2:24).
scriptureSignificance: Hezron's significance lies in his position within the genealogy of Judah, a tribe central to the Messianic line culminating in Jesus Christ. Being a direct descendant of Judah through Perez situates Hezron within the covenantal promises given to Israel. His inclusion in the list of those who went to Egypt highlights his role in the formation of the Israelite nation during the Exodus period. References to the Hezronite clan further emphasize his legacy within the tribal structure of Israel.
